## Overview

LRPITT13B is the **SES-adjusted available-case modified-ITT** analysis for letter-sound knowledge (YARC-LSK) (`yarclet`)—the SES-robustness companion to LRPITT07. It uses the uniform specification plus linear adjustment for parental education (`MUMEDUPOST16`, `DADEDUPOST16`) and age first exposed to books (`AGEBOOKS`). Requesting these covariates imposes an additional SES complete-case restriction beyond the outcome-specific observed-data requirement; LRPITT14b is the matched unadjusted comparator on exactly those rows, so LRPITT13B versus LRPITT14b isolates adjustment with the selected sample held fixed. The estimand is the assigned-arm contrast in $L_{\text{post}}$ in that SES-complete fitted sample. A causal reading requires the archive, outcome and SES complete-case selection not to induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked causal DAG, $G$ is a randomised root, so the offer contrast in the original full randomised cohort requires no baseline-covariate adjustment. Restricting to archived children with observed outcome and SES variables can break that exchangeability; a causal reading of $\tau$ in this complete-case sample requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes, while extension to all 57 requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity. The own baseline, linear age and SES adjusters are **precision terms only** — they may sharpen $\tau$ but do not identify effects after selection. **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the intervention arm has the higher modelled outcome.

## Model

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \text{logit}_*(L_{\mathrm{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i} + \sum_{c \in \text{SES}} \gamma_c\, z(c_i),
$$

with Beta-Binomial likelihood $L_{\text{post},i} \sim \text{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu_i\kappa, (1-\mu_i)\kappa)$,
$\mu_i = \sigma(\eta_i)$, $N = 32$. Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
The SES adjusters enter as linear $\gamma_c$ terms (the same weak $\text{Normal}(0, 0.3)$ prior as cross-baseline couplings); HSGPs are off by default.
